harness: Roo Code (VS Code extension RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline + Roo Code CLI)
vendor: Roo Code Inc. (RooCodeInc) — spin-off/fork of Cline, same core engine
binaries: VS Code extension `RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline` (src/package.json: name="roo-cline", publisher="RooVeterinaryInc", version 3.53.0). CLI: npm `@roo-code/cli` v0.1.17, bin name `roo` (apps/cli/package.json). The CLI is NOT named `roocode` — Discodex's existing `Provider::from_executable` already maps "roo"|"roocode"|"roo-code" -> Provider::RooCode, so "roo" is covered.
surfaces: VS Code extension (and VS Code forks: Cursor, Windsurf, Trae, VSCodium, Code - Insiders) + standalone CLI (npm @roo-code/cli, bin `roo`). Both surfaces write the SAME on-disk task format; only the storage root differs. No JetBrains plugin, no standalone desktop app.

paths: VS Code extension, Windows: %APPDATA%\<VSCodeApp>\User\globalStorage\rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline\tasks\<taskId>\api_conversation_history.json  (DO NOT READ — raw conversation)
<VSCodeApp> = Code | Code - Insiders | Cursor | Windsurf | Trae | VSCodium  (i.e. %APPDATA%\Code\User\globalStorage\rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline\tasks\ for stock VS Code)
Roo Code CLI, Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.vscode-mock\global-storage\tasks\<taskId>\ui_messages.json (and history_item.json in same dir)
Roo Code CLI --ephemeral: %TEMP%\roo-cli-<ts>-<rand>\global-storage\tasks\<taskId>\ (deleted on exit; default is NOT ephemeral)
Escape hatch: VS Code setting `roo-cline.customStoragePath` can relocate the whole extension storage root (src/utils/storage.ts getStorageBasePath).
NO per-project subdirectory: ALL tasks live flat under tasks/<taskId>/; project grouping is by the `workspace` field inside history_item.json.
storage.format: JSON, one file per task. ui_messages.json = a SINGLE JSON ARRAY of ClineMessage objects (packages/types/src/message.ts schema: {ts,type:"ask"|"say",ask?,say?,text?,reasoning?,partial?,isAnswered?,images?,progressStatus?,contextCondense?,contextTruncation?,checkpoint?}). history_item.json = a single JSON object. tasks/_index.json = {version,updatedAt,entries[]}. api_conversation_history.json = single JSON array of Anthropic MessageParam. NOT JSONL. ripgrep over the whole upstream tree for ".jsonl" returned ZERO matches. No SQLite, no protobuf, no encryption, no auth token required, no cloud-only component. The IDE's own globalStorage dir also contains VS Code's state.vscdb (SQLite), but Roo Code's task data does NOT live there since 3.49.0 — so no sqlite crate is needed.
storage.append_semantics: NOT APPEND-ONLY. This is the decisive constraint. Every write goes through src/utils/safeWriteJson.ts, which (1) serialises the WHOLE array to a sibling temp file `.<name>.new_<ts>_<rand>.tmp`, (2) renames the current file to `.<name>.bak_<ts>_<rand>.tmp`, (3) renames the temp file onto the target (atomic replace, NEW INODE), (4) unlinks the backup. Writes happen LIVE during a run: Task.ts addToClineMessages() -> saveClineMessages() on every single message, and say() re-saves on every partial->complete transition. Consequence: the target file is REPLACED WHOLESALE, its byte length can grow OR SHRINK, it contains no newlines at all, and transient .new_*.tmp / .bak_*.tmp files appear next to it. Discodex's existing LogTailer (byte-offset cursor + newline splitting) is INVALID for this format: it would mis-frame partial content, re-emit stale bytes, and can never parse a single-line JSON array. A dedicated whole-file/snapshot reader is required.
storage.session_file_naming: Task id = UUIDv7 (src/core/task/Task.ts:454 `this.taskId = historyItem ? historyItem.id : (taskId ?? uuidv7())`); the task directory is named exactly that UUID. Files inside: ui_messages.json, history_item.json, api_conversation_history.json, task_metadata.json (legacy), settings.json (Cline only). Flat index file: tasks/_index.json. Project grouping is NOT directory-based — it is the `workspace` (absolute cwd) string inside history_item.json plus the `status` field (active | delegated | completed) and parentTaskId/rootTaskId links for sub-agent (new_task) sessions.

fields.project: RECOVERABLE. history_item.json -> "workspace" = absolute cwd of the task. Discodex must publish only project_name(cwd) (final folder name). NOTE: history_item.json also contains "task" = the USER PROMPT — must never be read. Also "mode" (architect|code|ask|debug|orchestrator) and "apiConfigName" (user-authored provider profile name — not publishable raw).
fields.model: NOT RECOVERABLE. Roo Code does not persist the selected model id in any task file. api_conversation_history.json is an array of Anthropic MessageParam ({role,content,ts,...}) with no model field; history_item.json has only apiConfigName (a local provider-profile nickname, user-authored, not a model id). There is no local record of the model used for a task. Consequence: the Discord presence cannot show a model/agent name for Roo Code; the richest honest substitute is the Roo mode (fixed whitelist architect|code|ask|debug|orchestrator) surfaced as AgentDetected.
fields.file_basename: RECOVERABLE. The tool "ask" message's `text` is JSON.stringify(ClineSayTool) whose `path` is already RELATIVE to cwd (getReadablePath(task.cwd, relPath)). Read only `path` (or `batchFiles[0].path` for batch reads) and take the basename. DANGER: the same JSON also contains `content` (for write_to_file it is the ENTIRE new file body; for read_file it is the ABSOLUTE path) — never read `content`.
fields.tool_activity: RECOVERABLE. Token vocabulary from the `tool` field of ClineSayTool (packages/types/src/vscode-extension-host.ts): readFile, editedExistingFile, newFileCreated, appliedDiff, listFilesTopLevel, listFilesRecursive, searchFiles, codebaseSearch, switchMode, newTask, finishTask, updateTodoList, runSlashCommand, skill, readCommandOutput, generateImage, imageGenerated. Shell commands arrive as {type:"ask", ask:"command", text:"<raw shell command>"} — classify with the existing classify_tool() helper, never publish the command. MCP tools: ask:"use_mcp_server". No tool-call id exists in Roo Code, so the tracked variants (TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished) cannot be used; use plain ToolStarted/ToolFinished.
fields.phase: RECOVERABLE. say:"api_req_started"/"api_req_started"->Thinking, say:"reasoning"->Thinking, say:"text"->Thinking, ask:"followup"->Thinking (waiting for user), say:"command_output"->ToolFinished, say:"completion_result"->TerminalCandidate, ask:"completion_result"->Completed, say:"subtask_result"->ToolFinished.
fields.timestamps: RECOVERABLE, epoch MILLISECONDS. ClineMessage.ts = Date.now() (number). Messages are stored in creation order, so the array is ordered. Task start = ts of ui_messages.json[0] (the first message is always the task say — see taskMetadata() `taskMessage = messages[0]`). NOTE: history_item.json "ts" is NOT the task start; it is the ts of the LAST relevant message.

parser_strategy: New branch `Provider::RooCode => parse_roo_line(line)` in src/events.rs::parse_line_for. The reader feeds ONE JSON OBJECT per "line" (a whole-file snapshot reader re-serialises each array element to a single line), so the parse_line_for one-line contract is preserved. Discrimination inside parse_roo_line is by shape, not by filename: if the object has a "workspace" string it is a HistoryItem; if it has "type" in {"ask","say"} it is a ClineMessage. Mapping: (a) HistoryItem -> SessionMetadata{project: project_name(workspace), cwd: workspace}; optionally AgentDetected from a FIXED whitelist map of `mode` (architect|code|ask|debug|orchestrator) — never publish `task` (the prompt) and never publish `apiConfigName` raw. HistoryItem must NOT emit TaskStarted (its "ts" is the last message time, not the task start). (b) ClineMessage ask:"tool" -> parse `text` as JSON (ClineSayTool), read ONLY `tool` and `path`/`batchFiles[].path`; map the token to a fixed safe label (appliedDiff|editedExistingFile|newFileCreated -> "Editing files"; readFile|listFilesTopLevel|listFilesRecursive -> "Reading project files"; searchFiles|codebaseSearch -> "Searching project"; switchMode|updateTodoList -> "Planning changes"; newTask -> "Running coding agent"; readCommandOutput -> "Reviewing terminal output"; generateImage|imageGenerated -> "Inspecting image"; runSlashCommand|skill -> "Using development tools"; unknown token -> "Using development tools", never echo the token) and set ToolActivity.file = basename(path) + language_from_file; emit plain ToolStarted (no call id exists in Roo Code, so TrackedToolStarted cannot be used). (c) ClineMessage ask:"command" -> `text` is the RAW shell command: emit ToolStarted with label = classify_tool("execute_command", text) and file=None — the command text itself must never escape. (d) ask:"completion_result" -> Completed; ask:"followup" -> Thinking{reasoning:None}; ask:"use_mcp_server" -> ToolStarted{"Using MCP tool"}. (e) say:"api_req_started"|"api_req_finished"|"reasoning"|"text"|"user_edit_todos" -> Thinking{reasoning:None} (Roo's reasoning is unstructured prose, so do NOT run extract_reasoning_summary on it — pass None to guarantee no model text leaks); say:"command_output"|"subtask_result" -> ToolFinished; say:"completion_result" -> TerminalCandidate; every other say/ask value -> emit nothing. (f) Any malformed JSON, missing fields, or unknown vocabulary -> empty event list (fail closed).

risks: NOT append-only / not line-delimited. ui_messages.json is a single-line JSON array that is atomically REPLACED (new inode) on every message via a temp-file rename. Discodex's LogTailer (byte-offset cursor + newline splitting) is structurally invalid for it and MUST be replaced by a whole-file snapshot reader — this is the single biggest engineering cost and the main reason this needs custom machinery.

Transient sibling files .<name>.new_*.tmp and .<name>.bak_*.tmp are created and deleted during every write; a naive exact-filename matcher is safe, but a prefix/extension matcher would parse half-written temp files.
The file is REPLACED, not appended, so its length can SHRINK (partial->complete mutation, checkpoint restore, overwriteClineMessages). Any index-based diffing must reset when the array shrinks.

The tool payload JSON contains genuine secrets: `content` holds the ENTIRE new file body for write_to_file and the absolute path for read_file; `diff`/`originalContent` hold full file contents; `reason` holds a code snippet; `query`/`searchPattern` hold user text. A parser that reads anything but `tool` and `path` leaks file contents to Discord.

history_item.json contains the raw USER PROMPT in the `task` field. It must be read for `workspace`/`mode` only. api_conversation_history.json contains the entire conversation and must never be opened by Discodex.

The model id is NOT persisted anywhere locally, so Discodex can never show a model for Roo Code. If the presence is expected to name a model, this adapter will look poorer than Codex/DSH no matter how good the parser is.
Task.setPartialMessage mutates the last array element in place (partial -> complete) without changing its ts, so a pure index-diff reader silently loses the final update of the last tool message.

Two different storage roots (VS Code %APPDATA% globalStorage vs the CLI's ~/.vscode-mock) plus arbitrary VS Code forks plus the `roo-cline.customStoragePath` setting means the adapter needs N roots and cannot assume one fixed path. A missing root must degrade to the existing focused-app detection, not to "no presence".
No per-project directory: all tasks are flat under tasks/<uuid>/, so the "newest N logs" heuristic in recent_logs() counts tasks, not projects, and needs de-duplication by task directory.

No call_id in Roo Code's format, so the TrackedToolStarted/TrackedToolFinished machinery cannot be used; tool-finish detection falls back to say:"command_output" heuristics, which can be late for auto-approved tools.
user-authored custom mode slugs and apiConfigName strings appear in history_item.json; publishing them raw would leak arbitrary user text into Discord, so they need a fixed whitelist.
confidence: High on the file layout, format, and write semantics (all read directly from the upstream Roo-Code tree at main/HEAD b867ec9, and cross-checked against the released tags v3.30.0 and v3.53.0). High on the VS Code globalStorage path (full upstream chain from microsoft/vscode). High that the model id is not persisted (no model field in ClineMessage, HistoryItem or ApiMessage). Medium on the exact per-message tool-token -> label mapping for a few rare tools (readCommandOutput / imageGenerated tokens were inferred from the ClineSayTool union, and I did not trace every tool's runtime payload). Low confidence only on the `roo-cline.customStoragePath` relocation, which is documented in the manifest but not exercised by the adapter. No local machine data was read — every claim comes from upstream repositories.
summary: Roo Code DOES write a rich, local, machine-readable activity store — but NOT in a shape Discodex can consume today. It is a per-task directory of JSON files, and the activity file `ui_messages.json` is a single JSON ARRAY that is atomically REPLACED (whole-file rewrite via temp-file rename) on every message, not an append-only JSONL stream. There is no .jsonl anywhere in the upstream repo and no SQLite/protobuf/encryption. Everything needed for a Codex/DSH-level presence IS recoverable WITHOUT conversation text: workspace folder name (history_item.json -> "workspace"), current file basename (tool ask payload -> ClineSayTool.path, already relative to cwd), normalized tool activity (ClineSayTool.tool token -> fixed safe label), phase (ask/say discriminators), and the elapsed timer (ClineMessage.ts, epoch ms). The MODEL id is the one gap: Roo Code never persists the selected model locally, so the presence cannot name a model. Net: viable and rich, but it needs a NEW whole-file snapshot reader in watcher.rs (the existing LogTailer is structurally invalid here) plus a new parse_roo_line branch in events.rs. The Roo Code CLI stores the identical format under a completely different root (%USERPROFILE%\.vscode-mock\global-storage\tasks). Relative to Cline the layout is materially IDENTICAL (same ui_messages.json / api_conversation_history.json / tasks/<taskId> layout); Roo's additions are the per-task history_item.json + tasks/_index.json (since 3.49.0), the CLI, and the roo-cline.customStoragePath escape hatch.
